To solve the inequality $\frac{x + 6}{x^2 + 2x + 7} \ge 0$, we first need to analyze the denominator. Since the denominator $x^2 + 2x + 7$ is always positive for all real values of $x$ (as we can verify by analyzing the discriminant, the quadratic equation $x^2 + 2x + 7 = 0$ has no real roots because the discrimen of this quadratic is $2^2 - 4 \cdot 1 \cdot 7 = -24$, which is negative), then the sign of the fraction will be determined by the numerator alone.

The numerator is $x + 6$. We are on the search for the values of $x$ that make this expression non-negative (i.e. greater than or equal to $0$).
